newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MARCH 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The start of trading this week at the Athens Stock Exchange - following a tumultuous week in which record gains turned into record losses - finds foreign investors reserved, Greek institutional investors divided about whether to buy and private investors absent. The clumsy move by the administration of the bourse is obviously to blame for the sudden turnaround in fortunes but experts say the market still has much to offer the long-term investor.

--The government is reported to be considering a reduction in the working week with a subsequent reduction in pay for the private sector in an attempt to create jobs. The proposal is expected to be brought up during "social dialogue" with the Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) and the General Confederation of Workers of Greece (GSEE).

--High social security contributions by workers and employers to the Social Security Foundation (IKA) and to public organisations is in direct contrast to the level of services and are a factor contributing to tax evasion. In some cases, contributions can total up to 51 percent of workers' incomes.

--The lack of the appropriate infrastructure for ship repairs and building is the major reason why shipowners are failing to bring their vessles to the Peramatos shipyard zone. Now a 26-point proposal to support the zone and reduce regional unemployment is under consideration.

--The government wants a flourishing and prosperous stock exchange which will allow businesses to invest capital and bolster growth, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papapandoniou says. National Bank of Greece Governor Theodoros Karatzas says that Greece is facing the best macroeconomic balances for the last 25 years and that the general price index is capable of reaching 2,000 points.
--The non-payment of social security contributions to IKA is thought to run to the one trillion drachma mark: new legislation is planned to deal with employers evading payment.
--The insurance market is facing a new round of mergers and buyouts with banking-insurance groups strengthening their positions and radically changing the scene.

--Capital Market Commission President Stavros Thomadakis says he had informed National Economy and Finance Minister Papandoniou of his intention to warn small investors last week and insists he would do it again.

--The national economy ministry and Greece telecoms organisation OTE last week decided on the sale of a share package that will raise 250-300 billion drachmas for the organisation. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
